verdictRationale: The spec closes the original dotted-path and overclaimed-atomicity problems in intent, but the new normalized-schema fragment introduces a JSON Schema `oneOf` conditional bug that can make valid records fail validation. This is fixable by changing the conditional composition, but it blocks PASS because the schema is load-bearing for P1 and AC13.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A normalized fixture with status disabled, no source.content_hash, and no doctor object fails schema validation, or an installed fixture with required hash and doctor fields fails validation because both oneOf branches validate vacuously.
falsifiability.observableSignal: The schema validator reports a oneOf match-count error instead of accepting the otherwise valid normalized record.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Run the normalized schema validator against two minimal positive fixtures: one disabled record with no doctor/content_hash and one installed record with source.content_hash plus doctor.last_run_status. Inspect whether validation succeeds and whether any oneOf branch-count error is emitted.
falsifiability.threshold: Both positive fixtures must validate successfully with zero oneOf branch-count errors.

newIssueList.title: Conditional oneOf branches validate vacuously
newIssueList.description: The normalized schema fragment uses `oneOf` containing `if`/`then` branches without an `else` or a branch-local `required: ["status"]` plus `const` guard. In JSON Schema, when an `if` condition is false and no `else` is present, that subschema still validates. As written, a valid `status: disabled` record can satisfy the disabled branch and also vacuously satisfy the non-disabled branch, causing `oneOf` to fail; the same risk applies in reverse for installed/broken/declared records.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Use `allOf` with two independent `if`/`then` conditionals, or make each `oneOf` branch explicitly require and constrain `status` inside the branch schema so exactly one branch can match.
newIssueList.lineRef: Capability Records: declared vs normalized / Normalized schema oneOf

ledgerReview.rationale: The declared versus normalized split still prevents hand-authored registries from requiring computed content_hash values.
The status lifecycle remains clearly separated between operator intent in declared registries and derived status in generated artifacts.
The per-type required field table and absent-only forbidden semantics still address the overfit single-schema shape.
The three secret gates remain concrete and cover structural, named-secret, and entropy-based leak modes.
Dry-run now has a stable redirected output tree and doctor checks run against the dry-run artifacts.
The prose now intends disabled records to omit content_hash and doctor, but the new oneOf encoding can still make valid disabled normalized records fail validation.
Adapter emission happens after doctor resolves final statuses and writes only to staging before promotion.
The spec now states forbidden fields must be absent and present-but-empty fails validation.
The dotted-path bug was removed, but the replacement schema fragment has a different JSON Schema composition bug that still undermines enforceability.
The spec now accurately scopes promotion to per-file atomicity and adds generation markers, doctor detection, fault tests, and recovery.

preserveList.summary: The spec now honestly models adapter promotion as per-file atomic with explicit mixed-generation detection and resume recovery.
preserveList.lineRef: Harness adapter generation / Atomicity model and AC14

preserveList.summary: Disabled records are now conceptually represented without source.content_hash or doctor and remain visible in inventory while excluded from adapters.
The generated versus hand-edited artifact boundary is clear enough to preserve deterministic installs and prevent registry mutation.
